claims.text: Incorporating machine-learning models that account for interactions among multiple principal elements can improve prediction accuracy for high-entropy-alloy melting temperatures.
Such machine-learning models can improve the computational efficiency of melting-temperature prediction relative to traditional methods.
The intervention can improve prediction of melting properties other than melting temperature.
Interactions among the multiple principal elements in high-entropy alloys are complex.
Machine-learning models can capture nonlinear relationships between high-entropy-alloy composition and melting properties.
Capturing nonlinear composition–property relationships leads to improved melting-property prediction accuracy.
The proposed performance depends on training the models using a large and diverse dataset of high-entropy alloys with known melting properties.
The hypothesis remains valid for high-entropy alloys containing up to 10 principal elements.
Model performance may be affected by the quality of the training dataset.
Model performance may be affected by the diversity of the training dataset.
